name: curl
one_line: Send exactly the HTTP request you describe and show exactly what comes back.
plain: Send exactly the HTTP request you describe and show exactly what comes back.
The sections below show when to use it, real examples, and the options explained in plain English.
when: Test a web challenge without a browser: change a header, cookie, method or body and see the response.
Download a file, follow a redirect, check a status code in a script.
Reproduce what Burp or the browser sent, as a copy-paste command.

examples.output:

examples.title: Change headers and send a cookie
examples.output:
GET /
User-Agent: MyAgent/1.0
Accept: */*
Referer: http://natas5.example

examples.title: POST a form and JSON
examples.cmd: curl -s -d 'user=alice&pass=1' http://127.0.0.1:8099/login; echo; echo ----; curl -s -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"a":1}' http://127.0.0.1:8099/api

User-Agent: curl/8.5.0
Accept: */*
Content-Length: 17

user=alice&pass=1
----

User-Agent: curl/8.5.0
Accept: */*
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 7

{"a":1}

examples.title: Basic auth is just base64
examples.cmd: curl -s -u alice:secret http://127.0.0.1:8099/ | grep Authorization; echo 'YWxpY2U6c2VjcmV0' | base64 -d; echo

examples.title: Redirects
examples.cmd: curl -si http://127.0.0.1:8099/old | head -3; echo ---; curl -sL -o /dev/null -w 'final=%{url_effective} code=%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8099/old
examples.output:
HTTP/1.0 301 Moved Permanently
Server: BaseHTTP/0.6 Python/3.12.3
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 19:12:22 GMT
---
final=http://127.0.0.1:8099/new code=200

examples.title: Status code only, for scripting
examples.cmd: for p in / /admin /missing; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$p %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:8099$p; done

options.plain: Silent / show errors even when silent
Include response headers / HEAD request only
Verbose: show the request and response headers
Set the method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
Request body (form data) / URL-encode a value
Send JSON with the right headers (recent curl)

options.use: Basic-auth pages (note: it is only base64)

options.plain: Save the body to a file / use the remote name
Print a field after the transfer
Do not squash `/../` in the URL

mistakes: Quote URLs that contain `&` or `?`: the shell treats `&` as 'run in background'.
`-d` implies POST and `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`; use `-G` to put data in the URL instead.
Use `--data-urlencode` for values with spaces or symbols, or they are sent raw.
curl may normalise `/../` in the URL; add `--path-as-is` to send it unchanged.
`-k` disables certificate checks: fine for your own lab, never for real credentials.
try: Send the request that makes the lab echo header `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1`.
Write a loop that prints the status for 10 paths from a list in a file.
Reproduce a browser request from DevTools: right-click, Copy as cURL.
see_also: wget, httpie, Burp Repeater, ffuf, nc (raw HTTP), python requests.
